about: The one place that says what is built. Pages and the README read this file. A feature may be 'built' only if 'verify' (a command anyone can run) and 'proof' (a file in this repository) are filled in. To flip a feature: edit its status here, then run: python3 tools/site.py build && python3 tools/site.py sync-readme && python3 tools/site.py check

features.name: Memory that carries over
features.plain: What an agent fixed or decided comes back in a later session, with a record of where it came from.
features.exists: TRACE, our public search that shows its work, is the memory. One small recorded test exists: a helper asked TRACE 20 questions over our full test library, and a hidden checker with 23 rules accepted the recorded answers. The command that stores a fix in one session and brings it back in a new one does not exist yet.
features.will: `anima memory put "decision: retries stay at three"` stores a decision or a fix. In a new session, `anima memory ask "how many retries?"` brings it back with the text and a record id that points to where it came from.
features.limit: A small local store, not the 100-million-token library. It aims at continuity (the agent knows what was decided before) and makes no claim of better fixes. The 20-question test is a small sample.

features.name: Works inside your harness
features.plain: ANIMA works inside the coding tool you already use (the harness): Muse Code first, then Claude Code, then Codex.
features.exists: Nothing is wired yet. The three tools have command-line modes, and ANIMA's adapters are meant to call them.
features.will: `anima run --harness muse --task examples/tiny-bug` sends one small bug task to Muse Code and ends with the hidden checker's verdict. The same task goes to Claude Code or Codex by changing one word.
features.limit: Thin adapters and a tiny task first. Blocking a forbidden action before it runs is expected to work first on Claude Code, which has per-action hooks. On Muse Code and Codex ANIMA starts with a wrapper and a process watch.

features.name: Muse Code
features.plain: The first harness. Muse Code runs the task and ANIMA wraps it with the hidden checker and the rules.
features.exists: Muse Code already did the small-model work in the recorded nine-job run (it said done nine times, seven were right). That run used our earlier driver, not the new plug-in.
features.will: `anima run --harness muse --task examples/tiny-bug` ends with `VERDICT PASS` and exit code 0.
features.limit: Tiny task only. The tool must already be installed and logged in on your machine.

features.name: Claude Code
features.plain: The second harness. The same task, sent to Claude Code, judged by the same hidden checker.
features.exists: Claude Sonnet fixed both wrong answers in the recorded run, as the second rung of the ladder. That run used our earlier driver, not the new plug-in.
features.will: `anima run --harness claude --task examples/tiny-bug` ends with the checker's verdict.
features.limit: Tiny task only. The tool must already be installed and logged in.

features.name: Codex
features.plain: The third harness. The same task, sent to Codex, judged by the same hidden checker.
features.exists: Codex is the last rung of the recorded ladder; it was not needed in the nine-job run.
features.will: `anima run --harness codex --task examples/tiny-bug` ends with the checker's verdict.
features.limit: The run may end as NOT RUN if Codex is not installed and logged in on the machine. Tiny task only.

features.name: One line to install
features.plain: One command sets ANIMA up in a private folder, with no admin rights, then checks which of your coding tools it can find.
features.exists: Nothing to install yet. Today you clone the repository and run the record check (see Try it).
features.will: One line installs ANIMA into a private folder and a small Python environment. Then `anima doctor` lists which of Muse Code, Claude Code and Codex it found and writes a starter `anima.yaml`.
features.limit: The tools must already be installed and logged in. The one-line address only works after the project's first push to GitHub, so a clone is the way in until then.

features.name: One screen: the State Space Tree
features.plain: Every agent, task and attempt on one screen, drawn as a tree you can follow. SST stands for State Space Tree.
features.exists: The recorded nine-job run exists as a decision log with 69 records, which is what the screen reads. The screen itself is not built yet.
features.will: A web page. The root is the mission, the branches are tasks, the leaves are attempts coloured right, wrong or waiting. An escalation adds a branch. It first replays the recorded nine-job run, then follows a live run.
features.limit: It draws the decision log, not what a model is thinking. One computer.

features.name: Talk to it
features.plain: Say what you want. Speech is turned into text on your own computer, with local Whisper.
features.exists: Nothing is built yet. The plan uses faster-whisper, a local speech-to-text library, running on the CPU.
features.will: `anima voice --file voice/samples/status.wav` prints what it heard and the command it understood, for example {"cmd":"status"}. Starting or stopping a task needs a typed confirmation.
features.limit: About six fixed English commands. Shown first from a recorded clip, because a microphone can fail inside WSL. The delay has not been measured.

features.name: Roles and enforced rules
features.plain: Architect, manager and worker; secrets, no-push and budgets; a hidden checker; a tamper-evident record. The professional discipline behind the rest.
features.exists: Three of five parts exist in some form: the hidden checker and the ladder (one job type, recorded run) and the tamper-evident record (anyone can check it). Roles and the rules pack are designed, not built.
features.will: One file, `anima.yaml`, holds roles, permissions, budgets, watches and the ladder, so it works on any harness.
features.limit: Designed from how we actually run our own work. ANIMA has two of ten of those controls today.

features.name: Roles and a mission file
features.plain: Architect, manager, worker: who may do what, written in one file.
features.exists: The roles and the file format are written down as a design. Nothing reads the file yet.
features.will: Each role gets a list of what it may do, what it must not do, and a budget. Every task card must point to a line of the mission and name a file as its test.

features.name: Rules that are enforced
features.plain: A small rule pack that blocks secrets, sudo, pushing to a public repository and deleting protected files. A program enforces it, not the agent's good intentions.
features.exists: We run a larger version of this on our own work. It is not part of ANIMA yet.
features.will: `anima check --cmd 'cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519'` prints `block` and exits with code 3.
features.limit: Blocking before the action runs is proven only on Claude Code, which has per-action hooks. Budgets are in the design, not in this first pack.

features.name: A hidden checker judges every answer
features.plain: Tests the agent cannot see or edit decide whether an answer is right.
features.exists: Validated on one kind of job (fix a bug, judged by hidden tests): in a recorded run of nine real jobs, seven answers were right the first time and two wrong "done" answers were caught.
features.will: The same checker runs inside `anima run` for any harness.
features.limit: One kind of job. The checker's code is not in this repository yet, so only the record of the run can be re-checked from here.

features.name: A wrong answer climbs to a stronger helper
features.plain: When the checker says no, the next helper gets the task plus the one failing line: a small local model, then Claude Sonnet, then Codex.
features.exists: In the recorded run both wrong answers went one rung up to Claude Sonnet, which fixed them. The Codex rung was not needed.
features.will: The ladder runs inside `anima run` across the harnesses you have installed.
features.limit: The second helper was told the failing line, so it was an informed retry, not a blind one. One run, nine jobs.

features.name: A record nobody can quietly edit
features.plain: Every decision is one line in a log, and each line carries a fingerprint of the line before it, so an edit shows.
features.exists: The 69-record log of the nine-job run, a checker script anyone can run in a second, and a page that does the same check in your browser.
features.limit: The seal shows the record was not changed afterwards. It cannot show that the run itself was honest. The check does not re-run the nine jobs.
features.expect: recorded run: CHAIN OK - 69 records, every link matches, then: edited copy: CHAIN BROKEN - 69 records, line 7 does not match the line before it
features.needs: Python 3 and git; about 11 MB; about one second
